headline: "Can't hold on any longer" as cost pressure drives food makers to raise prices in succession
summary: Food companies in South Korea are raising prices in succession as cost pressure and a heatwave weigh on the industry, even after the won-dollar rate recovered more than 100 won. Samyang Foods will freeze its product prices this year.
why: Food and beverage makers are sensitive to input costs such as raw materials, energy and currency moves, and their pricing decisions feed into consumer inflation.
